D2a-03-nucleotide-molecular-structure

A single nucleotide drawn as three joined simple shapes: a yellow circle for the phosphate group, a pale orange pentagon for the deoxyribose sugar, and a coloured rectangle for the nitrogenous base attached to the sugar. Beside it, four small rectangles in four distinct colours representing the four bases (green, red, blue, orange).
D2a-05-mitosis-versus-meiosis-comparison

Side-by-side flow diagrams comparing mitosis and meiosis, starting from a parent cell containing two pairs of chromosomes (one long pair and one short pair; in each pair one chromosome red from the mother and one blue from the father). Left column "Mitosis": parent cell → chromosomes duplicated and lined up singly at the equator → two daughter cells each with the same four chromosomes (two red, two blue) as the parent. Right column "Meiosis": parent cell → homologous chromosomes paired up, with crossing over shown as swapped red and blue segments → first division separating pairs → second division separating chromatids → four daughter cells each with only two chromosomes (one long and one short), in different red/blue combinations.
D2a-08-monohybrid-cross-punnett-square

Monohybrid cross diagram for tall and dwarf pea plants in three tiers. Top tier (P): a tall pea plant and a dwarf pea plant with a multiplication sign between them. Arrows down to gametes shown as small circles. Middle tier (F1): four identical tall plants. Bottom tier (F2): a 2 by 2 Punnett square with T and t along the top and side; three squares contain small tall plant icons and one square contains a dwarf plant icon.
D2a-09-genetic-test-cross

Two side-by-side test-cross diagrams. Left: a black guinea pig crossed with a white guinea pig "bb", producing four black offspring. Right: a black guinea pig crossed with a white guinea pig "bb", producing two black and two white offspring.
D2a-10-incomplete-dominance-cross

Incomplete dominance cross in four-o'clock flowers. Top: a red trumpet-shaped flower crossed with a white flower. Middle (F1): pink flowers. Bottom (F2): a 2 by 2 Punnett square with R and W on the top and side; the squares show one red flower, two pink flowers and one white flower.
D2a-11-abo-inheritance-punnett-square

Punnett square for ABO inheritance: father group A (genotype I^A i) on the left, mother group B (genotype I^B i) on top, with gametes I^A and i down the side and I^B and i across the top. The four squares contain small coloured blood-drop icons: purple for AB, blue for A, green for B and white with red outline for O.
D2a-12-sex-determination-inheritance

Sex determination diagram. Top: a woman icon labelled with chromosome pair XX and a man icon labelled XY. Arrows to gametes: the woman produces two egg circles each containing X; the man produces one sperm with X and one sperm with Y. Crossing arrows to four children icons at the bottom: two girls labelled XX and two boys labelled XY. Use pink for X chromosomes and blue for the Y chromosome.
D2a-15-albinism-inheritance-pedigree-chart

A simple family tree (pedigree) over three generations using standard symbols: squares for males and circles for females, joined by horizontal marriage lines and vertical lines to children. Generation I: an unshaded square (normal father) and an unshaded circle (normal mother). Generation II: four children: an unshaded square, a fully shaded circle (girl with albinism), a half-shaded circle (carrier daughter) and an unshaded square. Generation III: the carrier daughter married to an unshaded square has two children, an unshaded circle and a fully shaded square.
D2a-01-chromosome-dna-structure

Diagram of a single duplicated chromosome shaped like an X, made of two identical side-by-side sister chromatids joined at a constricted centromere. Show the chromatids coloured soft purple, with faint horizontal bands. On the right, draw an enlargement (zoom lines from part of one chromatid) showing the chromatin uncoiling: a coil of fibres, then beads of protein (histones) on a string, then a DNA double helix. A short coloured band on one arm marks a gene.
D2a-07-mendel-pea-plant-traits

A chart of Mendel's seven pairs of contrasting characters in pea plants, arranged in seven rows with the dominant form on the left and the recessive form on the right. Row 1: tall pea plant vs dwarf pea plant. Row 2: round smooth seed vs wrinkled seed. Row 3: yellow seed vs green seed. Row 4: purple flower vs white flower. Row 5: inflated pod vs constricted pod. Row 6: green pod vs yellow pod. Row 7: flowers along the stem (axial) vs flowers at the stem tip (terminal).
D2a-14-ishihara-colour-blindness-test

A circular Ishihara-style colour vision test plate made of many small dots of different sizes: the background dots in shades of orange, yellow and brown, and a hidden numeral 7 formed from green and olive dots. Beside it, a smaller second circle showing how the same plate appears to a red-green colour-blind person, with all dots in similar muddy yellow-brown shades so the number cannot be seen.
D2a-02-human-male-karyotype

A simplified human male karyotype: 22 pairs of purple X-shaped chromosomes arranged in rows in decreasing size, numbered 1 to 22, plus a final pair consisting of one medium X chromosome and one much smaller Y chromosome, highlighted in blue.
D2a-13-haemophilia-sex-linked-pedigree

Haemophilia inheritance diagram for a carrier mother and a normal father. Top: mother icon with chromosome pair X^H (normal X in pink) and X^h (X with a red dot marking the haemophilia allele); father icon with X^H (pink) and Y (blue, shorter). Gametes shown as circles below each parent. A 2 by 2 Punnett grid below with four child icons: normal girl X^H X^H, carrier girl X^H X^h (half-shaded), normal boy X^H Y, haemophiliac boy X^h Y (fully shaded red).
D2a-04-dna-ladder-helix

Two views of DNA side by side. Left: an untwisted section of DNA drawn as a straight ladder, with two vertical sugar-phosphate backbones (alternating yellow circles for phosphate and orange pentagons for sugar) and horizontal rungs made of paired coloured bases: A (green) with T (red), G (blue) with C (orange), with dotted lines between each pair for hydrogen bonds; show two dotted lines in A–T pairs and three in G–C pairs. Right: the same molecule twisted into a smooth right-handed double helix with coloured rungs.
D2a-06-monohybrid-gene-transmission

Monohybrid inheritance genetic diagram on a white background. 

Top row shows parents: left circle labelled "Father (Aa)", right circle labelled "Mother (Aa)". 

Arrows pointing down to second row show four gamete circles: two sperm ("A", "a") on the left; two eggs ("A", "a") on the right. 

Arrows connect gametes to a bottom row of four zygote circles labelled "AA", "Aa", "Aa", "aa":
- Leftmost sperm "A" connects to zygotes "AA" and the first "Aa".
- Sperm "a" connects to the second "Aa" and zygote "aa".
- Leftmost egg "A" connects to zygotes "AA" and the second "Aa".
- Egg "a" connects to the first "Aa" and zygote "aa".

Every zygote receives exactly one arrow from a sperm and one from an egg. Clear spacing, simple flat circles.
